issues.legal_issue: A finding on title in an earlier proceeding bars a later title determination only when title was directly and substantially in issue and was heard and finally decided.
material_facts: A person claiming ownership brought a later suit seeking a determination of title after an eviction suit in a Small Causes Court.
The defendant in the eviction suit had filed a written statement claiming ownership, but the Small Causes Court’s decision did not refer to that pleading or address title.
The later suit directly raised the question of title.
issues.conclusion: Res judicata did not bar determination of title in the later suit because the earlier court had not addressed or decided title.
issues.legal_principle: Under the principle in Gangabai w/o Rambilas Gilda v. Chhabubai w/o Pukharajji Gandhi, a matter bars a later suit as res judicata only if it was directly and substantially in issue in the earlier suit and was heard and finally decided. A finding that is merely collateral or incidental does not suffice.

predicates.later_suit_seeks_title: A party brought a later suit seeking a determination of rights in property based on title.
predicates.earlier_case_was_small_causes_eviction: The earlier proceeding was an eviction suit before a Small Causes Court.
predicates.prior_title_issue_was_not_adjudicated: The earlier court did not address or decide the title issue, even though a party had raised a claim of ownership.

issues.definition: When a later suit seeks a title determination after an eviction proceeding and the earlier court did not adjudicate title, res judicata does not bar that determination.

issues.legal_issue: A court’s disposition is not binding as a decree on a party when it does not adjudicate the matters in controversy by stating the points for determination and deciding them.
material_facts: A party to an eviction suit filed a written statement claiming ownership of the property.

The Small Causes Court’s brief decision treated the suit as uncontested, did not refer to that party or the written statement, and stated no points for determination or findings on the contested matters.
The later dispute concerned whether that decision bound the party whose pleaded claim had not been addressed.
issues.conclusion: The Small Causes Court’s decision was not a judgment or decree in law and was non est as far as the party whose claim it had not addressed was concerned.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(2), 2(9), and 2(14) of the Code of Civil Procedure distinguish a decree, judgment, and order; a decree or order requires an adjudication that conclusively determines rights in controversy. Order XX Rules 4(1) and 5 require points for determination and decisions on them, while Order XIV Rules 1 and 3 concern the issues to be determined. Under Section 17(1) of the Provincial Small Causes Court Act, the Code applied to the Small Causes Court in this case, and that court was required to state the points for determination and its decision on them.

predicates.effect_of_small_causes_disposition_is_in: A later dispute concerns whether a Small Causes Court’s disposition binds a party to the earlier proceeding.
predicates.party_filed_defense_claiming_ownership: A party filed a defense claiming ownership of the property.
predicates.prior_decision_omitted_points_and_findin: The earlier court’s decision did not state the points for determination or give findings on the matters raised by that party.

issues.definition: When the effect of a Small Causes Court disposition is disputed, a party raised ownership in a defense, and the decision omitted points and findings on that dispute, the disposition is not binding on that party.
